what_this_is: Asset -> {issuer list, per-ledger adapter} as data. The reader (scripts/readers/cross_ledger_funds.py) reads ONLY what this file names. Every deployment identifier is parsed out of the issuer page bytes at run time; no identifier is typed here. Endpoints are public keyless operators; 'operator' is who runs them. Adding an asset or a ledger is a data change.
rules: The deployment list comes only from the issuer's own public page. If no issuer-published list exists, issuer_list.state is ISSUER_LIST_UNAVAILABLE and nothing is read - explorers and aggregators are not issuer lists.
A token on a ledger the issuer itself describes as private/permissioned is PERMISSIONED_NOT_READABLE with the issuer's own sentence and source; it is not UNMEASURED-by-omission.
Products that share an issuer page but are different instruments (e.g. BENJI vs iBENJI) are kept apart; sums are per product and per evidence kind only.

avalanche.observed: 2026-09-25 probe: Ava Labs' public RPC does not offer eth_getProof; PublicNode and dRPC return proofs whose root node is not the block header's stateRoot, and PublicNode's headers carry settledHeight/settled* fields (possibly asynchronous execution, where a header commits to an earlier settled state - not established here). Header hash is not recomputed by this reader for this header format.

evm_slot_candidates.rule: every candidate is read with eth_getStorageAt at the pinned block and compared with eth_call totalSupply(); a proof is attempted only when exactly one candidate matches. The candidate set is the search space, not an assumption about the layout.

benji.question: Is BENJI the same thing on every ledger Franklin Templeton's own contracts page says it lives on, and how much does each ledger's state say is issued?

issuer_reported.why: The fund's own monthly SEC Form N-MFP3 (Franklin Templeton Trust). It is the issuer's statement - the claim, not evidence of what any ledger holds.

reconciliation.controlling_record: the fund's share register kept by its transfer agent (named in the N-MFP3 read below)
reconciliation.why: No transfer-agent register is public. The issuer describes the on-chain token as a representation of fund shares; which record controls, and whether the two agree on any date, is not measured here.

jpmd.question: Does the deposit token at the address JPMorgan's own Kinexys page links resolve on Base as JPMD, and what issued supply does Base's state show?

reconciliation.controlling_record: JPMorgan's deposit ledger (a deposit token is a claim on a bank deposit; there is no transfer agent)
reconciliation.why: JPMorgan publishes no outstanding-balance figure for JPMD; the bank's ledger is not public.
